title: "Examples"
subtitle: "Every transform, rendered."
description: "One source div reused several ways by the extension: plain, shifted, truncated, remapped, into a styled container, and with variables filled in."
---

Everything below is produced by the filter as this page is rendered, from the sources defined at the top.
This site configures the extension in `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
div-reuse:
  limit: 3
  vars:
    project: "Quarto Extensions"
    author:
      name: "Mickaël Canouil"
```

## The sources

Two divs, defined once and reused throughout the page.

````markdown
::: {#house-style}
Commit early, commit often, and write the message for the reader.
:::

::: {#report}
# Findings

The first top-level block of the report.

## Method

The second heading, so shifting has something to move.

::: {#report-note}
A nested div with an identifier of its own.
:::
::::
````

::: {#house-style}
Commit early, commit often, and write the message for the reader.
:::

:::: {#report}
# Findings

The first top-level block of the report.

## Method

The second heading, so shifting has something to move.

::: {#report-note}
A nested div with an identifier of its own.
:::
::::

## A plain reuse

```markdown
::: {reuse="house-style"}
:::
```

::: {.border .rounded .p-3}

::: {reuse="house-style"}
:::

:::

## Shifting headings

The report starts at level one, which would sit above the headings on this page.

```markdown
::: {reuse="report" reuse-filter="shift-headings=3" reuse-take="2"}
:::
```

::: {.border .rounded .p-3}

::: {reuse="report" reuse-filter="shift-headings=3" reuse-take="2"}
:::

:::

Level one becomes level four and level two becomes level five, so both sit under this section.

## Taking part of it

`reuse-take` keeps only the first few top-level blocks.

```markdown
::: {reuse="report" reuse-take="2"}
:::
```

::: {.border .rounded .p-3}

::: {reuse="report" reuse-take="2" reuse-filter="shift-headings=3"}
:::

:::

The heading and the paragraph after it are kept, and everything below is dropped.

## Renaming identifiers

A plain reuse copies identifiers along with the content, which puts duplicates in the document.
`id-remap` renames them on the way in.

```markdown
::: {reuse="report" reuse-filter="shift-headings=3,id-remap=report-note->report-note-copy"}
:::
```

::: {.border .rounded .p-3}

::: {reuse="report" reuse-filter="shift-headings=3,id-remap=report-note->report-note-copy"}
:::

:::

The nested div arrives as `report-note-copy`, so the source keeps sole ownership of `report-note`.
Several mappings are separated by `;`.

## Reusing into a styled container

The destination keeps its own classes and attributes; only its children are replaced.

```markdown
::: {.callout-tip title="House style" reuse="house-style"}
:::
```

That one does not work, and the reference explains why: Quarto expands callouts before user filters run.
Put the callout in the source instead:

```markdown
::: {#tip-source}
::: {.callout-tip title="House style"}
Commit early, commit often.
:::
:::

::: {reuse="tip-source"}
:::
```

:::: {#tip-source}
::: {.callout-tip title="House style"}
Commit early, commit often.
:::
::::

::: {reuse="tip-source"}
:::

## Variables

Tokens in the source are filled in from `div-reuse.vars` when the content is reused.

```markdown
::: {#greeting}
Written for {{project}}, signed {{author.name}}.
:::

::: {reuse="greeting"}
:::
```

::: {#greeting}
Written for {{project}}, signed {{author.name}}.
:::

::: {.border .rounded .p-3}

::: {reuse="greeting"}
:::

:::

Dotted paths reach nested keys.
A name with no value is left as written and warned about once.
